transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-12-26 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Ravi Desai (Solstice ML), Emily Park (Solstice infra), Jonas Li (Solstice CTO)

Summary:
Short walkthrough of Redwood Optimize quantization profiles (INT8 vs FP8), discussion of quality vs latency tradeoffs for Solstice ML's summarization pipeline, Qs on VPC/private deployment and SOC2/KMS. Agreed to run POC with representative prompt set and share benchmarks.

Topics:
- Quantization profiles: INT8, FP8, mixed
- Quality regressions and evals
- Latency SLOs and batching strategies
- Dedicated vs hosted routing for production
- Security: SOC 2, KMS, audit logs, SSO

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, i'm joined by Arjun, our SE. how are you folks doing?
[00:08] Ravi Desai: Hey all, good, thanks, yeah excited to see what you have for quantization. we run a realtime summarization for legal docs so latency is pretty important.
[00:15] Arjun Patel: Great, thanks Ravi. quick agenda — we'll show the Optimize console, walk through INT8 and FP8 profiles, show quality vs latency curves and then talk POC next steps. feel free to interrupt.
[00:30] Emily Park: quick thing — infra side, we need to understand VPC and private routing, and also the KMS integration for keys.
[00:37] Maya Chen: absolutely. we'll cover that in the security section. quick question on target p50/p95?
[00:43] Jonas Li: aim for p95 under 300ms for single-turn summary requests, but p50 ideally < 120ms. cost is still a factor — we can't triple infra spend.
[00:52] Arjun Patel: understood. so in Optimize we typically run a set of quant profiles — baseline FP16/FP32, FP8, and INT8 — we measure quality on your eval prompts and latency on your predicted seq lengths. i'll share an example chart.
[01:10] Arjun Patel: (screen) here's a typical quality vs latency plot — x axis latency, y axis quality metric (we used Rouge-L in this example). FP8 sits very close to FP16 quality with ~20-30% latency improvement on A100-like hardware; INT8 gives larger speedups but sometimes a small quality delta depending on model and task.
[01:32] Ravi Desai: when you say small delta, like how big? we can't accept hallucination increases.
[01:38] Arjun Patel: totally — it depends. for our summarization test across 1k prompts we saw median Rouge drop of ~0.7-1.5 points for INT8 on some models, FP8 usually under 0.5. but some heads and logits layers can be sensitive — we include per-layer sensitivity in the profile.
[01:58] Emily Park: per-layer sensitivity, is that automated?
[02:03] Arjun Patel: yes, Optimize runs a profile pass on a sample corpus — it outputs a recommended config: which layers to keep in higher precision, where to clamp ranges, plus fallback thresholds. you can export profiles to run in your infra.
[02:18] Maya Chen: important note — the runtime supports automatic fallback to FP8/FP16 for tokens where quant error would be high, that's part of the graceful degradation we talked about earlier.
[02:29] Jonas Li: so for our traffic, which is variable doc lengths, would caching help? we often get repeated prefixes.
[02:36] Arjun Patel: yes, KV cache/prefix caching can reduce token compute for follow-on turns. also continuous batching reduces per-token overhead but trades off tail latency. we can model per-route batching policies.
[02:48] Ravi Desai: can you quantify the latency gains on the hardware we use? we mostly run on T4s and a few G5s for burst.
[02:57] Arjun Patel: T4 numbers are lower than A100/G5; INT8 helps a lot for throughput on T4s but absolute latency improvements are mixed. on G5/RTX-class hardware FP8 often hits best latency/quality sweet spot. We'll include both in the POC.
[03:15] Emily Park: what about determinism and eval reproducibility — quant can make outputs less stable, right?
[03:22] Arjun Patel: small variance is possible; we recommend running multiple seeds and diff-based quality checks. Optimize's eval harness supports batch runs and regression detection.
[03:31] Maya Chen: quick demo — switching to the Optimize console — here's the model catalog, we'll pick the Llama-like model you mentioned earlier in the intake form.
[03:45] Arjun Patel: clicking into quant profiles — you can see the baseline FP16 run, then FP8 optimized, and INT8 experimental. each profile has a slider for strictness and a suggested expected quality drop and latency improvement.
[04:02] Ravi Desai: i see an option to toggle per-layer precision?
[04:06] Arjun Patel: yes, and you can pin certain layers to FP16 for safety; Optimize will flag layers with high sensitivity.
[04:12] Jonas Li: how do we integrate this into our dedicated fleet? we want reserved capacity yes but with private endpoints.
[04:20] Maya Chen: Redwood Dedicated supports private routing and we can pin model versions to specific GPU pools. the same quant profiles export and run on Dedicated or Private deployments — the control plane gives you rollout configs.
[04:33] Emily Park: SOC 2 and audit — our security team will want KMS, SSO, and audit logs.
[04:38] Maya Chen: we have SOC 2, SSO via SAML/Okta, and audit logs; for Private deployments you can use customer-managed KMS/HSM and we keep detailed request and rollout audit events. we'll share the security deck.
[04:52] Ravi Desai: any known competitors that do this end-to-end?
[04:56] Maya Chen: a couple — some vendors offer quant pipelines but not the unified rollout and cost analytics. RunAI and MajorCloudAI have parts but customers tell us they need the integrated Eval+Optimize flow.
[05:06] Arjun Patel: jumping back to quality vs latency — here's an example table from a previous POC: FP16 baseline p95 latency 420ms, FP8 p95 330ms, INT8 p95 260ms; quality (our rouge metric) FP16 22.3, FP8 22.0, INT8 21.5. again task dependent.
[05:32] Ravi Desai: that INT8 drop looks bigger than we'd accept for production. can we use mixed profiles?
[05:37] Arjun Patel: yes mixed precision is the common approach — keep critical layers at FP16, quantize others. that often recovers most quality while capturing most latency gains.
[05:47] Jonas Li: how quickly can we iterate? our timeline for a pilot is early feb so we need results in Jan.
[05:53] Maya Chen: sounds good — we'll target a POC run in the first two weeks of January. action items below.
[06:01] Emily Park: on infra, do you provide the benchmark harness or do we run Redwood's harness against our fleet?
[06:06] Arjun Patel: we provide the harness and can also run tests in our hosted environment as a baseline. for Dedicated/Private we'll give you the harness and config.
[06:14] Ravi Desai: about cost — how do you show per-token economics across quant profiles?
[06:19] Maya Chen: Optimize has cost modeling — we estimate token costs by effective GPU time per token and queued overheads; you can simulate monthly spend given traffic distribution. we'll include a cost projection in the spreadsheet.
[06:30] Arjun Patel: note that batching and caching assumptions alter cost a lot; Optimize can run sensitivity analysis for a range of batching policies.
[06:38] Ravi Desai: great. question on fallbacks for critical failures — if INT8 path fails or triggers quality regression midrollout what happens?
[06:45] Arjun Patel: we have automatic rollback and traffic split rollouts — canary first, monitor evals on the canary traffic, and auto-fallback to safe profile if quality delta exceeds threshold. you can set thresholds per-route.
[06:57] Maya Chen: also we maintain model variant compatibility so you can route to alternative model (smaller/larger) if a pool is down.
[07:05] Jonas Li: ok that's reassuring. any impact to latency when we enable audit logs and request tracing?
[07:11] Arjun Patel: tracing itself is lightweight; storing logs to an external SIEM adds async overhead usually. we recommend sampling at higher rates for canary traffic.
[07:20] Emily Park: bandwidth and data residency — we need logs in EU for some customers.
[07:24] Maya Chen: for Private we can configure region-local logging; for hosted we have EU regions and can route traffic accordingly.
[07:32] Ravi Desai: fine. can we talk about the POC acceptance criteria?
[07:36] Maya Chen: recommended criteria: 1) p95 latency target within 20% of baseline but cost < baseline by X% (we'll set number), 2) Rouge/qual regression less than Y points, 3) Successful integration with your KMS and SSO, 4) No more than 1% failed requests during test window.
[07:55] Jonas Li: acceptable — we'll refine the numbers.
[08:00] Arjun Patel: i'll outline the test plan: we'll run 3 profiles (FP16 baseline, FP8 recommended, INT8 mixed) across your 1k prompts, capture latency distribution and quality diffs, run two seeds for nondet checks, and run canary with 10% traffic for 48 hours.
[08:18] Ravi Desai: sounds good. one last Q — how do you handle model updates and version pinning?
[08:23] Maya Chen: you can pin model versions in Redwood Console and create rollout policies for upgrades. optimize profiles are tied to model version hashes so you can avoid silent regressions.
[08:33] Emily Park: ok thanks.
[08:35] Maya Chen: yep. quick live note — i'll send the benchmark sheet and security docs after. Arjun will share harness.
[08:42] Arjun Patel: i'll also drop a sample export of a mixed-precision profile and an example inference config for Dedicated.
[08:52] Jonas Li: perfect.
[08:54] Ravi Desai: any costballpark for Dedicated?
[08:58] Maya Chen: we'll include rough pricing tiers in the email; Dedicated is committed capacity monthly pricing — we'll tailor to your expected QPS.
[09:07] Emily Park: thanks everyone, we need to loop in our security team after you send SOC2 docs.
[09:12] Maya Chen: understood.
[09:14] — Meeting wrap, recap of next steps and deadlines —
[09:16] Maya Chen: Recap: Maya sends quant benchmark spreadsheet + pricing by 2027-01-02; Arjun sends POC harness + example config by 2027-01-04; Ravi provides prompt set by 2027-01-05; schedule POC kickoff first week Jan.
[09:35] Jonas Li: sounds good. thanks all.

End of transcript.
